title: Platform Recovery exact-SHA convergence and closure

phases.objective: Add one exact-SHA durable Recovery Kernel convergence entrypoint plus final closure classification, connector two-phase rebind, and persistent Local Manager throttling recovery without activating Production from repository source.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Recovery is classified only from durable same-cycle server evidence; unknown outcomes and missing backup or functional readback fail closed.
steps: Accept only expected_sha from the caller.
Resolve the evidence pack through a server-injected resolver.
Verify exact SHA, durable inspection identity and evidence hash.
Verify all-role backup evidence and every required core recovery gate.
Classify unknown outcome before any success state.
Separate connector auth and rate-limit attribution as non-DB degradation.
Return a deterministic no-secret closure hash.
assertions: Caller-supplied readiness booleans are forbidden.
Missing server resolver fails closed.
Missing backup evidence cannot produce recovered.
Unknown outcome cannot produce recovered and automatic retry remains forbidden.
Functional catalog and response-chunk readbacks are mandatory core gates.
Closure evaluation performs no Production, database, provider, migration, grant, deployment or workflow mutation.
Non-DB connector/429 gaps do not trigger DB recovery replay.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: runPlatformRecoveryConvergence with server-injected durable store, step executors, and approval resolver
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The run advances in canonical order, stops before unauthorized mutations, persists evidence/idempotency, and cannot blind-retry unknown outcomes.
steps: Bind the run to one exact Production SHA and deterministic plan hash.
Require independent durable recovery-store methods before execution.
Execute read-only discovery before conditional baseline repair.
Resolve every consequential or bounded-mutation authority server-side and bind it to SHA/run/plan/step/idempotency.
Require same-cycle authority/readback evidence from every mutation executor.
Treat unknown mutation outcome as reconciliation-only and forbid a second mutation during reconciliation.
Run catalog, response-chunk, activation, connector, rate-limit, Local Manager and deployment parity gates before final activation.
assertions: Caller-supplied approval is forbidden.
Mutation executors are not invoked without server-resolved exact-step approval.
Approval replay across a different SHA/run/plan/step/idempotency binding fails closed.
Unknown-outcome reconciliation is readback-only.
Ordinary MCP catalog migration remains after baseline and grant readiness.
Credential rebind is conditional on credential_invalid and is not triggered by rate limiting.
The framework has no live executor wiring in this PR and performs no Production mutation by repository delivery alone.

e2e_journeys.actor: Production Recovery bootstrap authority and Local Manager recovery clients
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Exact-SHA bootstrap status/plan/apply-schema plus existing connector and Local Manager recovery paths
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The independent Recovery Control Store can become schema-ready without target-DB mutation; ambiguous connector commit outcomes require reconciliation; Local Manager preserves long throttling windows and distinguishes application vs upstream-edge rate limiting.
steps: Inspect exact Production identity and independent Recovery Control Store configuration without mutation.
Generate a deterministic schema bootstrap plan bound to the exact deployed SHA.
Permit only repository-owned Control Store CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements after typed confirmation and same-cycle readback.
Reject partial schema drift, stale plan hashes, target database mutation, raw SQL, provider controls and caller credentials.
Mark any connector exception after commit dispatch as unknown outcome unless mutation_performed=false is proven.
Reject connector phase receipts with fields outside registered phase-specific allowlists.
Preserve server Retry-After values above 300 seconds in durable Local Manager backoff, with local exponential jitter that never shortens the server cooldown.
Stop ordinary desktop polling on credential_invalid until relink; retain authorization_denied as a separate non-rotation backoff.
Attribute application-generated 429 responses explicitly and classify empty 429 responses without application evidence as upstream_edge.
assertions: Control Store bootstrap never creates a database or user and never modifies Runtime, Governance, or Runtime Persistence target databases.
Control Store schema apply is exact-SHA, plan-hash and typed-confirmation bound and performs same-cycle readback.
Connector timeout after commit dispatch is reconciliation_required and automatic retry is forbidden.
Nested credential material and unregistered safe-looking receipt fields are both rejected.
Retry-After greater than 300 seconds survives durable restart state up to the declared one-day safety ceiling.
401 produces credential_invalid with relink_required and stops ordinary polling; 403 produces authorization_denied without credential rotation.
Application 429 carries rate_limit_source=application; empty/no-app-evidence 429 is classified upstream_edge.
Repository delivery performs no Production runtime deployment, target DB rebuild, grant apply, ordinary migration, provider mutation, or secret rotation.
All eleven Control Store tables and their critical column/index/table properties are checked from the canonical DDL inventory.
An empty Control Store is eligible for creation; existing malformed tables and unavailable schema evidence fail closed.
Deployment identity drift after plan validation prevents the first DDL; mid-cycle drift or lost acknowledgement requires reconciliation without replay.
Configured server-managed binding is not reported as verified live readiness.

phases.objective: Keep live Production recovery closure blocked until exact deployed SHA, backup evidence, fresh durable inspection, server resolver wiring, governed repairs and same-cycle functional readbacks are proven.
